To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gradient based routing approaches (GBR-G and GBR-GBR) and the competing gradient based routing approaches are more efficient in terms of energy consumption and network life time when compared to other routing techniques.
The proposed Gradient Based Routing approaches (GB-GR and CB-GB) achieve better performance in term of network lifespan compared to the single-sink Gradient Based Routing approaches.
the proposed GB-GBRs and CB-GBRs techniques outperform the single sink GGR-G and GBR-G approaches in terms of network lifetime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the network lifespan of multiple sinks WSNs by proposing a novel gradient-based routing approach which takes into account the energy consumption balance of all the sensor nodes in the WSN.
the design and evaluation of a new GBR approach for multiple sinks-based WSNs that aims at maximizing the network lifespan.
the design of energy efficient and balanced routing protocols for WSNs with multiple sinks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new proposed approaches are able to improve the network life time in multiple sinks-based WSNs.
the proposed GB-GBRs and CB-GBRs routing protocols are the best approaches to be used when multiple sinks are used in a WSN.
the proposed approaches (GB-GR and CB-GB) achieve a better energy consumption balance in the network compared to the single base station approaches (GBR-G and GBR- C).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approaches can be considered as a good alternative to the single sink based approaches in multiple sink WSNs.
the proposed gradient based routing approaches are able to balance the traffic load among all sensor nodes in the multiple sinks based WSNs.
, the new gradient model for the multiple sinks case, in addition to the gradient based routing approach, has a great impact on improving the energy efficiency of the WSNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed gradient-based approaches are able to improve the network lifespan by 10% and 15% when compared to the original gradient-based approaches in single sink WNS.
the proposed approaches are able to achieve a better balance in the energy consumption among the different nodes in the network.
, the use of multiple sinks in WSNs can be an effective way to prolong the network lifetime and improve the network scalability.
